title: Learning 400 Lines of Poetry “by Heart”
displayName: Week 15 Thursday Learning 400 Lines of Poetry “by Heart”

meta.intro: 背了四百行诗后，“我”的生活渐渐地充满了诗意。

source.pdf: 初2第3辑初中时文阅读提分训练3+X第3辑8年级.pdf

content.v: On the first day of Grade 8, my classmates and I were greeted by Mr Lemke, our new English teacher. Mr Lemke was in his 30s, but with his thick glasses and
tweed
jacket, he looked like a college professor.
“I might ask any of you, at any time, to stand up and recite one of those lines,” he said.
At the age of 12, I had a rather restless heart. I couldn’t help wondering: How would I ever learn 400 lines of poetry?
As the days and weeks passed, we weren’t just asked to memorise the poems. Mr Lemke taught us to
appreciate
them with all our senses. He invited us to feel the
rhythm
and the
mood
One of our first poems was
To Autumn
by John Keats.
But Keats also reminded us not to think too much about the future: “Where are the songs of Spring? Ay, where are they? Think not of them, thou hast thy music, too.”
I’d lock myself in my bedroom and go over a poem line by line until I could recite it by heart.
Somehow, I made it through Grade 8.
But that fall, when the leaves started to turn their brilliant colours, I found myself reciting the lines, “Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness...”
It took me years to realise the gift Mr Lemke had given me. He showed me how to treasure poetry, and in doing so, he made poetry part of who I am.

sections.instruction: Fill in each blank in the article with a proper sentence given below. Each sentence can be used only once. Note that there are two more sentences than you will need.

content.v: It celebrated the season of “
mists
and
mellow
fruitfulness”.
When I entered high school, I still felt restless.
We learnt to understand their meanings and discover their messages.
I’m thankful now that Mr Lemke made me memorise 400 lines of poetry.
He told us that we’d be learning 400 lines of poetry by heart over the school year.
Naturally, we complained about having to memorise all those poems that year.
I’d wait nervously to see who Mr Lemke would call upon to stand and recite one of the poems.
